# Hybrid RAG with a Numeric Guardrail

<p style="font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',monospace; font-size:.8rem; letter-spacing:.02em;">
RAG · Postgres + pgvector · Full-text search · Rank fusion · FastAPI · 22 tests
</p>
:::

::: {.rh-section}
## The business question

A health plan's member service answers the same questions all day. How long do I have to
appeal a denied claim? What does the emergency room cost? How many telehealth visits are
free? The answers are in the member handbook, and an assistant can find them in seconds.

It has to get one thing right every time: the number. A wrong co-pay or a wrong deadline
is the expensive mistake, because the member acts on it.

Two things have to hold. The assistant finds the right passage even when the member uses
different words than the handbook. And it refuses to answer when it is about to state a
number the handbook does not contain.
:::

::: {.rh-section}
## The data

A fictional health plan handbook with **8 documents**: appeals, dental, emergency care,
maternity, mental health, out-of-network care, prescriptions and telehealth. It is split
into **21 passages**. It is fictional on purpose. The repository is public, and a real
plan's documents are not mine to publish. The structure is the one that matters in a real
handbook: limits, co-pays and deadlines.

The test set has **16 questions written in different words than the handbook**: "ER" where
the text says "emergency room", "therapy" where it says "therapist". Each question records
which document answers it, so retrieval gets a score.
:::

::: {.rh-section}
## Method, and why this one

**One Postgres table instead of a vector database.** Each passage is a row holding its
text, its embedding (pgvector, HNSW index, cosine distance) and a full-text column with
its own index. Re-loading a document is a delete and an insert in one transaction, so the
two searches never see different versions of it. For most companies this means no new
system to run, because Postgres is already there.

**Two searches, combined by rank.** Vector search finds paraphrases. Full-text search
finds exact terms, codes and names. Their scores live on different scales, so instead of
tuning a weight on 16 questions they are combined with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, which only
looks at each passage's position in the two lists.

**The guardrail fails closed.** Before an answer goes out, every number in it is checked
against the passages that were retrieved ($1,500.00 and 1500 count as the same number). If
one is missing, the service returns no answer, flags it as blocked and names the number.
For limits, co-pays and deadlines, no answer is cheaper than a wrong one.

**It runs without an API key.** A simple extractive answerer, which picks the best
sentence from the passages, lets the whole pipeline and its tests run offline. A hosted
language model gives the real answers when a key is set. In the same spirit, a deterministic embedder keeps the
tests repeatable, and the evaluation then runs again with a real embedding model,
bge-small-en-v1.5.
:::

::: {.rh-section}
## Result

Retrieval is measured in CI on every change, against a real Postgres 16 + pgvector
database. The figure below is hit@1: the share of the 16 questions where the right
document comes first.

| Embedder | Vector | Full-text | Hybrid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Simple hashing (lexical) | 0.75 | 0.81 | **0.88** |
| bge-small-en-v1.5 | 1.00 | 0.81 | **1.00** |

With a weak embedder, the hybrid beats both searches, because each one fixes misses of the
other. With a good embedder, vector search already gets all 16 right and the hybrid keeps
that. Full-text alone misses the paraphrases. Sixteen questions make a smoke test. The CI gate
(at least 0.8 with the top 3 passages) is there to catch regressions when the chunking,
the indexes or the query change.

The guardrail, as the tests check it. Ask *"How long do I have to appeal a denied
claim?"* The handbook says 180 days, the answer says 180 days, and it cites the appeals
document. Swap in a model that answers *"You have 90 days to appeal"* and the service
withholds the answer and reports 90 as unsupported.

The repository states its limits too. There is no reranker yet, the evaluation covers
retrieval and not answer quality, the full-text search is configured for English only,
and the guardrail does not check numbers written out as words.
:::

::: {.rh-section}
## Applied to your documents

This is the core of the
<a href="../oquant.html#packages">Reliable AI Assistant pilot</a>: your documents or tables
in place of the handbook, 20 test questions you approve as the acceptance criterion, and
the same rule that no number reaches a user without being found in the source.
:::

::: {.rh-section}
## Code

```{=html}
<p><a class="rh-btn rh-btn-primary" href="https://github.com/rhozon/rag-pgvector-hybrid">github.com/rhozon/rag-pgvector-hybrid</a></p>
```

With Docker and Python 3.12:

```bash
docker compose up -d
pip install -e ".[dev,embed]"
python -m rag.cli ingest data/handbook --reset
python -m rag.cli ask "How long do I have to appeal a denied claim?"
python -m rag.cli eval --k 1
pytest -v
```

The defaults need no API key and no model download. The suite has **22 tests**, the
Postgres ones included, and runs on every push together with the retrieval evaluation.
The README lists the design decisions, from the choice of index to why the full-text
query is an OR of terms.
:::
